rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Peek at the next module before adding a second exercise
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule about authoring discipline, not a checkable body-text property of the shipped files. M4 has two exercises (walk-and-send-off, set-the-markers-send-it-off) and M5 opens cleanly with its own Prework/Connections, no silent boundary break visible in the bodies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Between-module reading appears in two places
rules_evaluated.evidence: M4:68-78 '## Pre-reads before Module 5' lists Clean Code Is Steering, Entis/Klaassen 'Bread in the AI Sandwich', Verification asymmetry, Klaassen Definitive Guide. M5:6-10 '## Prework' repeats all four with matching one-line framing ('Optional prep while it's still running: read Clean Code Is Steering...; watch Laura Entis on Kieran Klaassen...; read Verification asymmetry...; read Compound Engineering...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module artefact contracts explicit at both ends
rules_evaluated.evidence: M4 maintainer table row 1: producing prompt 'Commit the current state…' names the stable identifier 'm4/<task-slug> branch at the short SHA... written into the protected Run coordinates block in task.md'. M5:38-40 'Set up the worktree' names the consuming side explicitly: 'fork the un-packaged session's starting SHA into a sibling worktree' and M5's maintainer table row 1 confirms 'Set up the Module 5 worktree prompt' reads the Run coordinates block and forks '../<repo>-m5' from the named branch+SHA.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session boundaries and working directories are designed, not implicit
rules_evaluated.evidence: M4:80-82 'Next': 'You pinned the starting point and recorded where this session lives, so a fresh session reads it straight from task.md.' M5:38-42 names the working directory explicitly ('a sibling worktree... This module's work... runs in the worktree') and gives rationale (gitignored files copied at fork so M1/M3 context travels). Meta block confirms canonical M4-new-in-original-repo / M5-new-in-worktree boundary.

M4 maintainer block carries a 3-row 'Artefact contracts' table (branch+SHA, filled gap entries, session transcript) each with stable identifier / produced-by / consumed-by columns. M5 carries an 8-row equivalent table covering the worktree branch, reference, plan.md, verifier, RUN-NOTES.md, CLAUDE.local.md, observations/, and session transcript.

M5's send-off happens in the same room/session as M4's read (no multi-day gap being bridged with a rescue callout at M5 open); no body-prose rescue callout appears at M5 '## Start here', and none is required since M4's artefact (a stopped or completed session) cannot be 'missing' the way a send-off's return can — M4:64 states explicitly 'A stopped session counts; the trace is the artefact.'

M4:62-66 '## Bring to Module 5': 'Come to Module 5 without a session that got some way into the task and you'll be scrambling for material while the read is already underway. Your call.' Matches canonical form; stakes are clock/exercise-based ('the read is already underway'), not peer-comparison; no next-module mechanics explained, no head-start prompts, no unearned vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session boundaries and working directories are designed, not implicit
rules_evaluated.evidence: M6:21-23 names the working directory explicitly and gives rationale for why it is the M5 worktree, not the original repo or a new fork: 'Both sessions are readable: the branches share .git, and each run recorded its transcript path.' Meta block confirms: 'M6 opens a fresh session in the M5 worktree at ../<repo>-m5 where both runs already live'.

M5 maintainer block's 8-row table and M6 maintainer block's 4-row table ('Two-run gap map', 'Recurring-work shapes', 'Stale-rule deletion', 'Workflow-skills handoff prompt') each carry stable identifier / produced-by / consumed-by columns.

M6:27-29 carries two consecutive blockquotes at '## Start here': one naming rescue moves ('nudge it once'; 'paste the packaged re-send... let it catch up while you read on') and one naming the accept-loss floor ('You lose a bit of value but you can still do this module's exercises. Despair not.'). M6 maintainer block has the required documenting note: 'M6 opener rescue + accept-loss callouts — deliberate exception to check_student_facing.md rule 5 (golden path only in body)... Future judges should not re-flag.'

M5:185-189 (flag:module:spot-gaps-build-the-loop) '## Bring to Module 6': 'A packaged session with substance... Come to Module 6 without the packaged session and you'll have one session to read where the exercise needs two. Your call.' Stakes are stated as an exercise-structural cost (one session where the exercise needs two), not room/peer comparison, and none of the three failure modes (next-module mechanics, head-start prompts, unearned vocabulary) are present. The line departs from the literal 'scrambling for Y while Z' template but preserves its clock-based-stakes intent; flagged below as a non-blocking observation for a maintainer, not a rule violation, since no named harm is present.
